text:
vp-eng: Quick follow-up from the all-hands runtime segment. A few leadership asks: how will canaries surface batching/caching regressions vs kernel perf wins? Also curious about prewarm strategy and KV eviction safety. Keep it punchy. @maya-eng-runtime @eli-eng-sre

maya-eng-runtime: Short answers: canaries run in layered checks: perf (p95/p50), correctness sampling, and resource anomalies. Kernels go first by default; batching & cache tweaks follow. Prewarm: we auto-run prefix-warm for hot routes during canary windows. KV eviction: conservative LRU with safety TTLs.

eli-eng-sre: Ops specifics: canary health gates = p95 delta <= +7% OR p95 absolute <= target (hosted p95 <200ms), error-rate delta <= +0.35% abs, correctness sample diffs <= 0.15%. Any gate fail -> auto rollback for that step. We'll also watch GPU memory growth and scheduler backpressure.

jamal-ml: Kernel note: some models may shift optimal batch sizes. We'll produce a per-model recommended batching table post-canary. Also flag models where prewarm increases peak memory.

sophia-product: Product asks: what's the customer-facing line about Dedicated pinning and prewarm? Need one-liners for the Console modal and release note.

maya-eng-runtime: Console one-liner: "You can pin a model variant per-route to avoid automatic runtime updates; we also allow enabling prewarm during canaries for lower cold-call latencies." Release blurb: "Opt-in kernel and batching rollouts staged with safety gates; Dedicated customers can pin variants."

ruth-customer-success: CS question: If prewarm runs during canary, will that affect billing or quotas for Dedicated customers? Need a short answer.

jamal-ml: Short: prewarm will be billed as normal inference traffic; for Dedicated reserved capacity it consumes committed throughput but we can isolate prewarm to a background pool on request. We'll include opt-out instructions.

eli-eng-sre: Additional ops detail: prewarm schedule = run lightweight prefix-warm tasks during low-traffic windows, default 02:00-06:00 UTC, configurable per-customer. KV eviction policy = LRU by default with a 48h safety TTL; evictions from canary variants won't affect stable variant caches.

maya-eng-runtime: Example rollout snippet for docs (short): ```json
{"rollout_steps":[{"name":"kernel-canary","traffic":5,"min_hours":12},{"name":"batch-cache-validate","traffic":25,"min_hours":24},{"name":"full-rollout","traffic":100,"min_hours":24}],"rollback_triggers":{"p95_pct_increase":7,"error_rate_abs":0.35,"correctness_pct":0.15}}```

ops-bot: scheduled: attn-tiling-prewarm-canary -> 2025-06-15 03:00 UTC (initial window 72h). Monitor: https://console.redwood.ai/mon/attn-tiling-prewarm-canary

vp-eng: Good. Action items: maya publish the prewarm + eviction FAQ + JSON snippet by EOD Tue; eli add the monitors and make prewarm opt-out flow; product + CS prepare Console copy and CS talking points. Ping me on PRs. :thumbsup:
